public_headline: NASA Gemini 5 Debriefing Cover Page Declassified From Confidential
public_tldr: This document is the declassification cover page for Part II of the Gemini 5 technical debriefing transcript, originally classified CONFIDENTIAL. The page itself contains no substantive content — the actual debriefing discussions, including reported visual sightings by the crew, are not present in this extracted material.
public_narrative:
This record is a single cover page from Part II of the Gemini 5 flight crew technical debriefing. Gemini 5 flew from August 30 to September 2, 1965, launching from Cape Kennedy, Florida. The debriefing transcript was originally stamped CONFIDENTIAL and was later declassified, with a declassification date of November 20 (the year is unreadable due to poor scan quality). The declassification appears to have been carried out under the authority of Executive Order 11652, though the OCR rendering of that reference is garbled.

Because this is an image-type document — a scanned photograph of the original page — very little usable text was captured during extraction. What survives is limited to classification markings and the declassification stamp. The substantive content of the debriefing, which according to the archive's metadata covers pages 157 through 220 and includes crew reports of visual sightings of debris, 'snow,' and 'glittering pieces,' is not present in this extracted material.

No conclusions, analysis, or agency assessments appear on this page. It functions solely as an administrative cover sheet recording the document's classification history.
public_caveats: This is only a cover page — none of the actual debriefing content is included in the extracted text.

References to crew sightings of debris and 'glittering pieces' come from the archive's metadata description, not from the extracted source text itself.
The declassification authority reference (likely Executive Order 11652) is partially garbled in the scan, so that attribution is only partially confirmed.
No named individuals, agency conclusions, or substantive findings are present in this material.
